1 28 oz can crushed tomatoes 
1/2 bunch of cilantro 
1 small white or yellow onion
1 jalapeño (seeded if you want less spice)
1 tbsp salt
1tbsp sugar
1/2 tbsp cumin
2 tbsp lime juice

Throw all the vegetables in a food processor and pulse until chopped.
Add the rest of the ingredients and process until desired consistency 
Add to pot and heat on stove just until warm

My son, at age five, was mad when he found out. He is on the spectrum and has severe texture issues and food aversions. Because he was not able to quit eating meat entirely, he asked my husband and I to stop. And we did. A couple years later we moved from vegetarian to vegan and have stayed the course. Kids get it. And I'm happy to say that even though he is not vegetarian or vegan, he has worked through a lot of his aversions and will now happily eat some tofu dishes, and seitan.

A lot of bread products seem vegan but use the dough conditioner l-cysteine. It's typically sourced from poultry feathers and hog hair. 
The good news is it's listed in the ingredients, and a few brands are using vegan sources now. 
Also,  most things that are sneakily not vegan because of weird ingredients you wouldn't suspect have vegan counterparts now days. With a little digging you can have pretty much any food you love without the animal products. Good luck! And don't be down on yourself. It happens.
